title: KV Bank Layering + Batch Coalescer: Memory Orchestration for Long-Window Llama/Mistral/Qwen
creator: Aisha Rao
description:
Problem statement: Long-context variants of Llama/Mistral/Qwen are exposing two related bottlenecks in production: (1) inefficient KV residency causing GPU memory pressure when many simultaneous long-history sessions are live, and (2) continuous-batching heuristics that either over-delay (hurting latency SLOs) or under-coalesce (wasting throughput). This ticket proposes a combined approach — 'KV Bank Layering' paired with a 'Batch Coalescer' — to produce model-specific memory profiles that reduce peak GPU allocation while preserving latency SLOs and generation throughput.

Goals: 
- Reduce per-GPU peak memory for long-window workloads by 15–35% across target model variants (Llama-70B longctx, Mistral-32K, Qwen-32K) without increasing median P50 latency by >10ms.
- Maintain end-to-end throughput (tokens/sec) at >=95% of baseline when latency SLOs are honored.
- Provide deterministic, per-model tuning knobs that can be surfaced in the console (e.g., kv_bank_count, bank_eviction_thresholds, coalescer_delay_ms).

Design summary: 
1) KV Bank Layering: Partition KV cache into ordered banks (hot -> warm -> cold) where residency is decided per-layer using a lightweight score: recency * layer_importance_factor + layer_attention_density. Each bank has an occupancy cap and eviction policy tuned per model variant. Layering rationale: earlier layers tend to be accessed more frequently for short prefix reuse; later layers have sparser reuse patterns for long-context tokens. By storing later layers in lower-priority banks (or compressed quantized banks), we reduce active working set.

2) Bank-specific representations: hot banks use full precision (FP16/AMP path), warm banks use an int8-like low-precision path (quantized-friendly memory layouts), and cold banks use a swapped/host-backed layout that can fallback to slower IO only under extreme pressure. Switching thresholds are per-model and discovered by offline profiler.

3) Batch Coalescer: Continuous batching engine that maintains a sliding window (max coalesce delay configurable) and groups requests by expected kv-footprint class (small/medium/huge) and model-version. The coalescer uses a conservative prediction of final sequence length (from tokens_left estimate) to avoid creating oversized batches which would violate memory caps. A micro-scheduler can elevate small requests into existing batches within a 10-25ms window when it predicts token-level GPU efficiency gains.

Tuning approach and per-model profile outputs: 
- Offline profiler produces a per-variant 'memory profile' file: bank_count, layer_importance_weights (comma-separated floats), eviction_percentiles, expected_prefix_reuse_distribution, recommended coalescer_delay_ms, and fallback_policy.
- Memory profile format is intentionally compact (single-line JSON blob delivered with model artifacts) and consumed by runtime at model load. Profiles will be versioned and included in the model catalog.

Experiments and results (summary): 
- Llama-70B longctx (64k synthetic replay traces): bank_count=3, layer_importance skewed towards low layers (weights ~ [1.0, 0.5, 0.2]) reduced active GPU allocation by 28% on average across mixed traffic (30% long sessions, 70% short), P50 latency increased by +6ms, throughput retained 96% of baseline.
- Mistral-32K: bank_count=2 + int8 warm bank gave 18% memory reduction with negligible latency change (P50 +2ms) on 8 GPU multi-tenant pool.
- Qwen-32K: enabling host-backed cold bank reduced peak OOMs in stress test by 67% (fewer evictions hitting fatal paths) at the cost of occasional tail latency spikes (P99 increased by 120ms) which were mitigated by a model-level fallback rule to route to dedicated capacity.

Instrumentation and metrics: 
- New runtime metrics: kv_bank_occupancy{bank,model,variant,instance}, bank_eviction_rate, coalescer_coalesced_batches/sec, coalescer_avg_delay_ms, predicted_vs_actual_batch_memory.
- Dashboards: longctx-memory profile view (per-model), coalescer heatmap (delay vs success), and evictions over time.

Implementation plan: 
Phase 1 (this ticket): build bank layering abstraction, offline profiler integration, and a prototype Batch Coalescer placed behind a feature flag for canary hosts. Deliverables: profile generator job, 2 runtime flags (banking_enabled, coalescer_enabled), perf harness run results, and initial dashboards.
Phase 2: A/B rollout, tune per-model defaults, console UI for profile override, automated fallback routing when cold-bank IO percentage > X.
Phase 3: expose profile tuning in Optimize suggestions and add cross-tenant sharing heuristics for Dedicated.

Risks & trade-offs: 
- Cold-bank IO will add tail latency; mitigation: auto-fallback to dedicated capacity or model variant with shorter context for requests exceeding a predicted footprint.
- Increased complexity in allocator; mitigation: keep the layer->bank decision deterministic and record signals for offline analysis.
- Per-model defaults may underperform on unseen workloads; mitigation: conservatively bias towards latency SLOs initially.

Testing plan: 
- Unit tests for bank allocations and deterministic eviction order.
- Integration tests for coalescer correctness (no request loss, correct sequence order).
- Perf tests with synthetic traces and real replay traffic (staging) covering 3 variants and mixed request-size distributions.

Artifacts and links: See links field for PRs, dashboards, and confluence spec.

Next steps: 
- Merge prototype PR behind flag (assigned).
- Run extended replay on Llama-70B longctx traces and collect bank occupancy heatmaps.
- Meet with console team to discuss profile exposure and rollback UX.
comments: 2026-02-21 - Initial design walkthrough with Runtime and Serving teams. Consensus: start with 2-3 banks and expand. Action: Aisha to produce offline profiler mock output by Friday.

2026-03-02 - Canary run on 6 hosts (banking_enabled=true, coalescer_enabled=true). Observed 22% drop in active allocated bytes; P99 latency increased by ~85ms on pathological trace (Qwen stress). Decided to add a fallback routing rule in the next PR.
2026-03-05 - Code review feedback from @Kenji: tighten locking in bank eviction path and add a fast-path for single-request batches to bypass coalescer. Will address in follow-up commit.
2026-03-08 - Added new metrics (kv_bank_occupancy and coalescer_avg_delay_ms). Dashboard stub: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/longctx-memory/kvlayering. Early view looks promising.

2026-03-10 - Performance summary: Llama-70B profile (bank_count=3) shows 28% memory reduction on mixed workload. Mistral-32K int8-warm bank reduces memory by 18%. Qwen tail impacts require routing fallback; planning canary rollback threshold of 2% of requests hitting cold-bank IO.
Next actions: finalize profiler artifact format, respond to Kenji's review, and schedule extended replay (48h) with real production traces in staging.
Blocking: need security sign-off for host-backed cold-bank IO path (access patterns + HSM/KMS confirm). Filed security question to SecOps (ticket SEC-2203).
